title: AI-DLC project workflow
description: The AI-DLC team's workflow for this repository: lifecycles and their stages, who hands off to whom, gates and their approvers, the clarify matrix and request routing. The orchestrator reads it on every request; when it is absent the plugin default applies. Check it with `node .ai-dlc/workflow.mjs validate`; change it with `/ai-dlc:workflow edit <change>`. Fixed guardrails (agent-manager's exclusive authority over agent artifacts, a freshly spawned agent-manager for changes to its own definition and skills, trust-but-verify, a handoff record at every boundary and every hand-back stored, the test gate hooks and the workflow gate, an orchestrator that only delegates, stage owners that never do another agent's job) are not configurable here.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so editors offer completion, hover documentation and validation. Keep `./workflow.schema.json`.

version.description: Format version of this file. Always 1.

agents.description: Which plugin agents take part, and which of the project's own agents join them.

disabled.description: Plugin agents this project runs without (bare ids, e.g. `brutal-critique`). Every stage, routing entry and clarify entry that names a disabled agent must be removed or reassigned. `orchestrator`, `agent-manager`, `brutal-critique`, `sqa-engineer` and `code-reviewer` (which review every agent-artifact change: docs, and code) cannot be disabled.

custom.description: The project's own agents, by id, usable as stage owners, hand-off targets and clarify targets. Each must exist as `.claude/agents/<id>.md` or `.github/agents/<id>.agent.md`. Custom ids keep their own name; the orchestrator adds the `ai-dlc:` prefix only to plugin agents.

description.description: What the agent does in this workflow, in one sentence.

gates.description: Gates by id (defaults: G1 Clarify, G2 Refine / Align, G3 Plan, G4 Approve, release go / no-go). A stage's `gate` is crossed when that stage ends.

lifecycles.description: Lifecycles by code. The keys of this object are the one authoritative list of lifecycle codes (the plugin default's are in templates/workflow.json; a project may add its own): routing, composite `segments`, the `{LIFECYCLE}` part of a run's handoff folder (`artifacts.handoffs`) and every skill refer to these keys and keep no list of their own. Each has either `segments` (a composite of other lifecycles, run in order) or `stages`, never both.

routing.description: How the orchestrator's request-routing picks a lifecycle or a single agent for each work item. A lifecycle the user names in the request always wins.

byType.description: Request type (Feature, Bug Fix, Security Fix, TechDebt, Testing, Review, Release, Agent Artifact) -> lifecycle code it runs by default. Custom lifecycles are also picked by their `pickWhen`. Every value is one lifecycle code except `Agent Artifact`, which is required and is a list of lifecycle codes (default `["AAWH", "AAWP"]`): exactly one with `variant: "plugin"` and at most one with `variant: "harness"`; the orchestrator picks one per change set by the variant rule (with no harness lifecycle, every change set runs the plugin one). The older single string `AAW` is refused: run `/ai-dlc:workflow upgrade`. The listed lifecycles are guarded by role: no `software-engineer` stage; at least one `agent-manager` stage; every starting stage is `product-owner`, `software-architect` or `agent-manager`; a `brutal-critique` stage loops back to an `agent-manager` stage (docs, on REVISE). The plugin variant also has a `sqa-engineer` stage (code, on failing tests) and a `code-reviewer` stage (code, on Blockers or Warnings, listing the `sqa-engineer` stage directly in its `after`) that loop back to `agent-manager`, and a `software-architect` and a `system-engineer` stage the `agent-manager` stage follows through `after`. A review stage's `when` is omitted or exactly `the change set contains docs` (`brutal-critique`) / `the change set contains code` (`sqa-engineer`, `code-reviewer`), case and spacing ignored. A disabled agent may own no stage of a listed lifecycle. The rules: the workflow skill's references/aaw-review.md.

Agent Artifact.description: The lifecycles of agent-artifact work, one per variant (default `AAWH` harness, `AAWP` plugin / mod).

agentArtifact.description: The folder lists the variant rule reads to pick the agent-artifact lifecycle for a change set: any code, or any path in `pluginPaths`, runs the plugin variant; docs only, every path in `harnessPaths`, the harness variant; anything else is asked. A path in both lists counts as a plugin path. The rule: the workflow skill's references/aaw-review.md.

harnessPaths.description: Path globs, relative to the repository root, of the harness: agents, skills, rules, instructions, commands, prompts, the workflow file, AGENTS.md. `**` matches any characters including `/`, `*` any except `/`, `?` one character except `/`.

pluginPaths.description: Path globs, relative to the repository root, of plugin and mod code: plugins, tools, tests (same glob forms as `harnessPaths`).

handOff.description: Work that needs no lifecycle -> the single agent it is handed to. Keys are kinds of work in plain words. `agent-artifact work` always goes to `agent-manager`.

routeImmediately.description: Request types that run before the human confirms the plan, then are reported. P0 bugs are always routed immediately as well.

clarify.description: The Clarify loop: whom a stage agent may ask when one of its inputs is unclear. `maxFailures` must be below `maxRounds`. File-only: no environment variable overrides these.

maxRounds.description: Rounds per stage (one batched request and its answers) before the stage is blocked and escalated to the human. Omitted: 2.

maxFailures.description: Rounds that end with the question still open the stage may have before it is blocked and escalated, even with rounds left. Must be below `maxRounds`. Omitted: 1, or `maxRounds` - 1 when that is lower.

matrix.description: Asking agent -> the agents it may consult and about what. `human` as a target means the question goes to the human through the orchestrator. An asker with an empty list consults no one.

agent.description: The agent to ask (bare id), or `human`.

about.description: The topics this agent answers for the asker.

documents.description: Who writes and who critiques the documents of stages marked `critique: true`.

writer.description: The agent that writes documents (default `documentation-writer`); a stage owner may write its own and still have it critiqued.

critic.description: The agent that critiques documents in parallel with the writer before a gate (default `brutal-critique`). `null` skips document critique — documents then reach gates unreviewed. It never removes the review of agent-artifact changes (the `AAWH` and `AAWP` lifecycles) or the handoff review (`handoffReview`).

axes.description: Review axes; one code-reviewer instance runs per axis, in parallel, each presented under its own heading. `standards`: conventions and code quality. `spec`: conformance to the frozen spec and its ACs.

handoffReview.description: The handoff review: `brutal-critique` reviews each handoff record of these lifecycles before its receiver starts (PASS / REVISE), under its own limits, row `handoff-review` of `node .ai-dlc/workflow.mjs rounds`. The reviewer is always `brutal-critique`, so it is not a setting. Independent of `documents.critic` and of the gate critique.

lifecycles.description: The lifecycles whose hand-offs are reviewed (default `AAWH`, `AAWP`); each must be a key of `lifecycles`.

maxRounds.description: The most review passes of one handoff record. Omitted: 2. Overridden by `AI_DLC_HANDOFF_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` (`env` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, then `.claude/settings.json`, then the process environment), never by the `AI_DLC_CRITIQUE_*` variables.

maxFailures.description: How many REVISE verdicts one handoff record may get before the review stops and the human decides. Overridden by `AI_DLC_HANDOFF_REVIEW_MAX_FAILURES` at the same levels. Must be below `maxRounds`. Omitted: 1, or `maxRounds` - 1 when that is lower.

artifacts.description: Where the lifecycles write their artifacts, relative to the repository root.

product.description: Folder for product briefs and stories.

specs.description: Frozen spec per feature; `<feature-slug>` is replaced.

handoffs.description: Folder for one run's records; `{LIFECYCLE}` (a key of `lifecycles`), `{YYYYMMDD}` (the run's start date) and `{feature-slug}` (kebab-case) are replaced. Braces here, angle brackets in `specs`, `narratives` and `plans`: `{feature-slug}` and `<feature-slug>` are the same slug. The folder holds the run state, one current version per session, named `run.v<major>.md` or `run.v<major>.<minor>.md` (`run.v1.md`, `run.v1.1.md`, `run.v1.2.md`, `run.v2.md`…, the highest current; `run.md` in a run from before versions); each handoff record, `{step}[.{sub}][.l{loop}[.{round}]][.{n}][.h{round}]-{from-agent}-to-{to-agent}.handoff.md` (`.h{round}` marks `brutal-critique`'s review of the record with the same step code, `handoffReview`); and each hand-back, the same pattern ending `.handback.md` with the two agents swapped. Agent IDs only, never persona names. Who writes each file in each orchestration mode, step numbering and verification: the `handoff` skill.

agentId.description: A bare agent id in kebab-case: a plugin agent (`software-engineer`, without `ai-dlc:`) or a custom agent from `agents.custom`.

approves.description: The artifact the approver signs off at this gate.

approver.description: `human`: the orchestrator stops and waits for the human's approval. `orchestrator`: the orchestrator approves on the human's behalf and records it in the handoff record. `none`: the gate is skipped, but the handoff record is still written and verified.

note.description: Anything else the approver should know.

variant.description: Only for the lifecycles named in `routing.byType["Agent Artifact"]`, where it is required: `harness` for docs-only changes to the harness (default `AAWH`), `plugin` for plugin and mod changes and any code (default `AAWP`).

kind.description: `primary`: the full lifecycle (AI-DLC). `segment`: a part of the primary lifecycle that can also run alone. `focused`: an entry point for bugs, refactors, tests or reviews. `custom`: a lifecycle this project added.

pickWhen.description: When request-routing picks this lifecycle, in plain words.

exitArtifact.description: What exists when the lifecycle is done.

segments.description: Composite lifecycle: the lifecycle codes it runs, in order, gate by gate.

stages.description: The stages, in order. Each starts after the stages named in its `after` (default: the stage before it).

note.description: Rules that apply to the whole lifecycle.

id.description: Stage id, unique within its lifecycle, e.g. `build`.

agent.description: The agent that owns this stage (bare id).

skills.description: Skills the owner runs in this stage, named in its brief (bare skill names). Each must be a plugin skill listed in `.ai-dlc/catalog.json` or a project skill in `.claude/skills/` or `.github/skills/`; `validate` fails otherwise.

produces.description: The artifacts this stage hands to the next one (paths or short descriptions). The orchestrator verifies each before the next stage starts.

after.description: Stage ids that must finish before this one starts — who hands off to whom. Omitted: the previous stage. `[]`: starts the lifecycle. Stages with the same `after` run in parallel. A stage skipped by its `when` counts as finished.

when.description: Run this stage only under this condition, in plain words (e.g. `the change touches UI`). The orchestrator decides and records the decision in the handoff. On the review stages of the Agent Artifact lifecycles (`AAWH`, `AAWP`) only one phrase is accepted per reviewer: `the change set contains docs` for `brutal-critique`, `the change set contains code` for `sqa-engineer` and `code-reviewer` (case and spacing ignored), or no `when` at all.

gate.description: Gate id (from `gates`) crossed when this stage ends.

loop.description: A refinement loop: work goes back to an earlier stage until the condition is cleared, or until the loop's `maxRounds` or `maxFailures` is used up; then the orchestrator stops, and with findings open the human decides whether to raise the limits for that run (further fix rounds count against them) or to stop or accept the findings. `maxFailures` must be below `maxRounds`. For a loop whose stage agent is `brutal-critique`, `sqa-engineer` or `code-reviewer`, the AI_DLC_CRITIQUE_*, AI_DLC_TEST_* and AI_DLC_CODE_REVIEW_* MAX_ROUNDS / MAX_FAILURES variables (`env` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, then `.claude/settings.json`, then the process environment) override these values (the workflow skill's *Loop limits*); `node .ai-dlc/workflow.mjs rounds` prints the values in effect.

on.description: What sends work back, in plain words.

maxRounds.description: The most review passes this step may run. Omitted: 2.

maxFailures.description: How many failing verdicts this step's reviewer may return before the loop stops and escalates, even with rounds left. A failing verdict is what the loop's `on` names (`brutal-critique`: REVISE or Majors on a PASS; `sqa-engineer`: a test that fails because the code is wrong; `code-reviewer`: what the loop's `on` names; Blocker or Warning in `AAWP`). Must be below `maxRounds`. Omitted: 1, or `maxRounds` - 1 when that is lower.

critique.description: Documents this stage produces are written by `documents.writer` (or the owner) and critiqued by `documents.critic` in parallel before the next gate.

note.description: Anything else the stage owner's brief must carry.
